map.coordinateBasis: The nomination marks the palace between the access road and the former Ontótóo market. Standard PMTiles identify the surrounding road, river and nearby footbridge. Tree cover obscures the roof and forecourt.

searchArea.marker: Second Palace symbol on the grove plan, west of the access road and east of the market
searchArea.method: Similarity fit of the nomination plan to the mapped footbridge, the access road fork and the two turns of the inner river bend.

placementTrial.basis: The georeferenced nomination marker defines a search center. The trial forecourt faces the PMTiles road to the east, supported only by the documented street approach. The site and direct approach remain obscured.

archiveSearchArea.result: Both oppositely signed orientations clear mapped features. The scan rectangles and the plotted Iledi symbol support the archive search area without establishing a footprint or the direction of the forecourt.
archiveSearchArea.note: The draft centers on the published scan coverage and faces approximately south, 173.7° true, following the best exterior panorama fit. The panorama pin differs from the archive center by about 167 m, and the interior panorama supports a different direction. The model envelope clears the mapped road and river at this trial position. The actual footprint, ground datum and bearing remain unresolved.

extentCheck.reasoning: The draft is longer than the nominal scan rectangle at this bearing. The archive says the scan is unregistered and the rectangle is approximate. It cannot be used as a surveyed model size.

roofReview.observation: The side photograph shows raised sheet corners at two parts of the adjoining roof. The porch photograph shows bands of bamboo laid in alternating diagonal directions with timber cross-battens.

limitations: Particular roof heights, bay widths, and floor and rear-wall geometry are interpreted from the visible exterior.
Sculptural forms are approximate. The model includes a photographed painted panel and posts seen through the grille.
The archive metadata and gridded Iledi symbol define an approximate search area. Forest canopy hides the exact roof perimeter.
The raised sheets, corrugated laps and alternating bamboo panels follow the side and porch photographs. Exact sheet laps, slat angles and the covered joints are reconstructed.

The draft centers on the published scan coverage and faces approximately south, 173.7° true, following the best exterior panorama fit. The panorama pin differs from the archive center by about 167 m, and the interior panorama supports a different direction. The model envelope clears the mapped road and river at this trial position. The actual footprint, ground datum and bearing remain unresolved.

The exterior panorama supports a roughly south-facing forecourt. Its camera pin is about 167 m from the scan-coverage center. The trial footprint and signed bearing still need geographic confirmation.

grilleSightline.interpretation: Camera-to-grille ray from the indoor view. Its easterly sightline supports investigating the east-facing trial. The viewing ray alone does not determine the forecourt axis. The station coordinates disagree with the scan coverage.

interiorPanorama.observation: The inner room shows sculpted plaster with light looping bands and stippling, contrasting ochre and dark pigments, and clustered carved timber supports. The recreated rear panel, motifs, and post locations are interpretive.

photos.observation: The projecting upper figure has a separate head and two extended arms. A lower reddish trunk and two pale tusks curve out below it.
The profile photograph shows the carved mass in front of the right gable. The tusks and upper figure emerge above the low sculpture in the forecourt.

elephantWing.interpretation: The master and three nearer tiers model the projecting figure, long arms, trunk and paired tusks. Dimensions, depth, and the hidden attachment to the gable relief are interpreted from the photographs.

exteriorPanorama.interpretation: On the panorama compass the left and middle roofs lie from north-northwest toward east-northeast. Their roof run and the photographed forecourt support a southerly direction. Earlier trials faced east and west.
exteriorPanorama.sensitivityBasis: Ray-to-roof-height estimate from two manually picked ridge tips. Varies reconstructed ridge heights, assumed camera height and effective field of view. The range describes the test parameters, with camera north registration and actual roof dimensions uncertain.
exteriorPanorama.sculpture: The upturned forearms converge on two stacked closed fists with weathered finger bands. The closely spaced hollow arms stand out in front of the left-gable relief.

waterlily.credit: Adunni Olorisha Trust and Adunni Osun Foundation
waterlily.observation: The Trust close-up shows a left-gable waterlily with a deep asymmetric spiral, raised terracotta lips and a recessed center beside the joined hands. The wider left-wing photograph fixes the relative position. The spiral section and depth are reconstructed.
